name: Apache Ivy
client: Apache Ivy 2.6.0 on the pinned Maven/Temurin image
auth: Use an access or reference token as the HTTP Basic password, with AW_USER equal to its subject. The subject needs read permission for installation and deploy permission for publication on the selected repository; token scopes cannot exceed that identity. The same clients also accept a user password when Basic password authentication is enabled. Use HTTPS.
fresh_home: Create a new AW_WORK with mktemp -d for every run; client configuration, downloads and caches in the commands stay under this directory. Do not reuse it to prove a fresh download. Remove the temporary directory after use.
prerequisites: Repository layout must be ivy-default; these patterns are not for Maven-layout repositories.
A Java runtime and the checksum-verified Ivy JAR from the pinned client image.
Python 3 is used only to extract the hostname.

configure.code:
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/home"
export AW_REPO_URL="$AW_URL/artifactory/$AW_REPO"
export AW_HOST=$(python3 -c 'import os,urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.urlsplit(os.environ["AW_URL"]).hostname)')
configure.note: AW_HOST is the hostname only, without port, used for the HTTP Basic challenge.

configure.code:
<ivysettings>
  <settings defaultResolver="aw"/>
  <credentials host="${aw.host}" realm="Artifactory Realm" username="${aw.user}" passwd="${aw.token}"/>
  <resolvers><url name="aw">
    <ivy pattern="${aw.url}/[organisation]/[module]/[revision]/ivys/ivy-[revision].xml"/>
    <artifact pattern="${aw.url}/[organisation]/[module]/[revision]/[type]s/[artifact]-[revision].[ext]"/>
  </url></resolvers>
</ivysettings>
configure.note: Save as $AW_WORK/ivysettings.xml without shell expansion; Ivy resolves aw.* JVM properties. This explicitly matches the registered ivy-default layout, which differs from Ivy's built-in default filenames.

publish.note: Publish to a local or one-node federated repository. Remote repositories are read-through caches; select the local deployment member when reading through a virtual.

steps.note: Publish the actual Ivy descriptor and JAR. The descriptor declares organisation org.acme, module widget, revision 1.0.0 and a jar publication.

install.note: Select a local, remote, virtual or one-node federated repository with read permission. Dependencies must also be available through that repository.

steps.note: The pinned client image provides /opt/ivy.jar. Credentials are runtime JVM arguments; do not expose process arguments in logs.

limitations: Remote and virtual repositories are read-only in this recipe; publish to the local member.
Each resolve needs a new cache and retrieve directory.

contains: Ivy resolves the exact bytes from a <class> repository
I resolve the ivy recipe with token "invalid-recipe-token"
